Great idea—here are exact measurements you can use for the sheet-pan lemon garlic chicken with potatoes and green beans. This will yield about 4 servings. If you’re cooking for 1 or 2, you can halve or even quarter the ingredients.

Sheet-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken with Potatoes and Green Beans (serves 4)

Ingredients
- 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 1.8–2.2 lb total)
- 1 lb small potatoes (Yukon Gold or baby potatoes), cut into 3/4-inch pieces (about 4 cups)
- 8 oz green beans, trimmed (about 2 cups)
- 3 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- 3 garlic cloves, minced (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)
- Zest of 1 lemon (about 1 teaspoon)
- Juice of 1 lemon (about 2 tablespoons)
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme or dried oregano (or 2 tablespoons fresh chopped if you have it)
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
- Optional: lemon wedges for serving

Instructions
1) Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large sheet pan with foil or parchment for easier cleanup.
2) Potatoes: In a bowl, toss the potatoes with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, and half the minced garlic (or a pinch of garlic powder). Spread in a single layer on the sheet pan.
3) Chicken: Pat the chicken thighs dry. Brush the skin side with 1 tablespoon olive oil, then season with 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Sprinkle with lemon zest and the dried herb you chose.
4) Start roasting: Place the chicken on the sheet pan on top of the potatoes, skin side up.
5) Roast 20 minutes.
6) Beans added: In a small bowl, toss the green beans with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of pepper (you can add a bit of garlic powder if you like). After the 20 minutes, scatter the green beans around the chicken on the pan.
7) Finish roasting: Return to the oven and roast 8–12 more minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) at the thickest part and the potatoes are tender. The greens beans should be bright green and tender-crisp.
8) Finish and serve: Remove from oven. Squeeze the juice of the remaining lemon over everything. Taste and adjust with a little more salt or pepper if needed. Serve with lemon wedges if you like.

Buying tips for the chicken
- Best option for this one-pan style: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs. They stay moist and get nice and flavorful.
- Alternatives:
  - If you prefer breast meat: you can use bone-in, skin-on chicken breasts (2 breasts for this recipe). They’ll need about 25–30 minutes total, but check with a meat thermometer—the target is 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part.
  - If you only have boneless, skinless chicken thighs, you can use them, but they tend to cook faster—start checking at around 18–22 minutes and watch for overcooking.
- What to look for when buying:
  - Fresh chicken should have no strong sour or sulfur smell, skin should be pinkish and moist, not gray or slimy.
  - If buying pre-packaged, check the “sell by” or “use by” date and choose the freshest you can find.
  - If you see a lot of liquid in the package, that’s a sign it’s aged or brined; you may prefer dry-packaged to control salt.
- Potatoes and beans:
  - Potatoes should be firm with no big sprouts.
  - Green beans should be bright green and crisp; avoid beans that are limp or discolored.

Tips if you want to adjust
- If you want to be extra flexible, this recipe is forgiving. You can swap in carrots for the potatoes or use asparagus instead of green beans (adjust cooking time a bit; asparagus will cook faster).
- To reduce cleanup even more, you can line the pan with parchment and reuse the same pan for another simple sheet-pan meal later in the week.
